title: Vaishnavi Sharma Follows India Comeback With Four Wickets in Four Balls
excerpt: The Madhya Pradesh left-arm spinner took 6 for 22 against Andhra Pradesh in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy, days after taking nine wickets in two ODIs against Zimbabwe on her India return.
body:
• Left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma took four wickets in four consecutive balls and finished with 6 for 22 for Madhya Pradesh against Andhra Pradesh in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy on Friday, November 6.
  • She became only the second Indian woman to take four wickets in four balls in a T20 match, after Humaira Kazi for Mumbai against Saurashtra in 2022.
  • Madhya Pradesh restricted Andhra Pradesh to 129 for 8 and won on a 99-run opening stand, with Anushka Sharma making 81.
  • The feat followed her India ODI comeback against Zimbabwe, where she took 4 for 39 and then a maiden five-wicket haul of 5 for 39 in consecutive matches.

Vaishnavi Sharma took four wickets in four consecutive balls for Madhya Pradesh against Andhra Pradesh in the Senior Women's T20 Trophy on Friday, November 6, finishing with 6 for 22 in a performance Hindustan Times reported and Apex Sports News detailed. The four-in-four made her only the second Indian woman to achieve the feat in a T20 match, after Humaira Kazi did it for Mumbai against Saurashtra in 2022.

How the Four-in-Four Happened

Sharma, a left-arm spinner, was introduced into the attack in the fifth over and picked up two wickets for 16 runs across her first three overs, according to the match account. Returning for the penultimate over, she was hit for six runs off the first two deliveries before taking a hat-trick and then a fourth wicket on the final ball of the over — four wickets in four balls to complete a six-wicket haul.

Andhra Pradesh were restricted to 129 for 8 in their 20 overs. Chasing 130, Madhya Pradesh were carried by a 99-run opening stand between Aayushi Shukla and Anushka Sharma. After Shukla was dismissed by Devika Kandregula, Anushka Sharma, who made 81, added an unbeaten 34 runs with Nuzhat Parween to guide Madhya Pradesh past the target.

A Comeback Built Away From the Team

The domestic feat arrived days after Sharma's return to India's ODI side against Zimbabwe. RevSportz reported that, having missed out on the World Cup squad, she used the time away from the team to work on her mental and physical strength, on control and consistency, and on repetition through single-wicket bowling drills.

"I got a good gap in which I was able to work on myself. I was able to work on my mental strength and physical strength."

— Vaishnavi Sharma, speaking at the post-match press conference, via RevSportz

Against Zimbabwe she took 4 for 39 in 10 overs in the second ODI, then followed it with 5 for 39 in the third ODI in Vadodara on Wednesday, October 28, Cricbuzz reported. In that third match, Zimbabwe were bowled out for 131 in 39.5 overs after opting to bat, and India chased it down at 133 for 2 in 17 overs, with Pratika Rawal unbeaten on 59 and Shafali Verma unbeaten on 51, to complete a 3-0 series sweep. Sharma's 5 for 39, in only her third ODI, was her maiden five-wicket haul in the format, and she finished the final two ODIs with nine wickets in total.

"When I played for Harman, I made my debut for the India team. That was a special moment for me. Now I am taking five wickets under Smriti. That is also a special moment for me."

— Vaishnavi Sharma, via RevSportz

Background and What It Means

Sharma is an Indian international left-arm orthodox spinner who was part of the squad that won the 2025 Under-19 T20 World Cup and was the leading wicket-taker of that tournament, according to the background in the match report. At 20, she now has a maiden ODI five-wicket haul, a nine-wicket return across two internationals, and a domestic four-in-four inside the same stretch of weeks.

For India's spin depth, that sequence matters more than any single spell. A bowler left out of a World Cup squad has returned with wickets in both international and domestic cricket, using, by her own account, a plan built on control, calm and repetition rather than chasing wickets. Her stated focus, reported by RevSportz, remains on staying in the present and continuing to learn — the next test will be whether she holds her place as India's fixtures continue.
